title: Liver and Bacon with Onion Gravy
subtitle: Lambs liver and back bacon in a rich onion gravy
excerpt: Thinly sliced lambs liver and crispy bacon in a deep, savoury onion gravy. A fast and filling British hob supper that is ready in under 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Classic British hob dish of lambs liver and bacon in onion gravy, a long-standing British pub and household staple.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The onion gravy can be made a day ahead. Cook the liver fresh just before serving.

content.text: Liver needs a hot pan and very little time. Cook it for too long and it turns gritty. Two minutes per side in a hot frying pan is all it needs. Get the onion gravy done first and keep it warm while the liver cooks.
Melt the butter in the saucepan over a low heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook for 15 minutes until very soft and golden, stirring often.

Stir 1 tablespoon of flour into the onions. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually pour in the beef stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add the Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes to thicken. Keep warm.
Heat the frying pan over a high heat. Fry the bacon for 2 minutes each side until crisp. Remove and keep warm.
Dust the liver slices in the remaining flour. Season well with salt and pepper.
Add the oil to the same hot pan. Cook the liver slices for 2 minutes on one side only. Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more. The inside should be just pink.
Serve the liver and bacon immediately. Pour the hot onion gravy over the top.

items.symptom: The liver is tough and gritty.
items.cause: It was cooked for too long or the slices were too thin.
items.fix: Slice liver to 1cm thick and cook for no more than 2 minutes per side in a very hot pan.

items.symptom: The gravy has lumps in it.
items.cause: The stock was added too fast, or the flour was not stirred well before the liquid went in.
items.fix: Whisk briskly as the stock goes in. Strain the gravy through a sieve if needed.

items.symptom: The liver sticks to the pan.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough when the liver went in.
items.fix: Get the pan very hot before adding the liver. It should sizzle loudly on contact.
